Formula SAE Electric Vehicle

RoleChief Engineer
OrganizationCooper Union Motorsports
TimelineSep 2023 to May 2026

I joined the FSAE team in my first year and worked on the mechanical side of the powertrain. From second year the team had no electrical lead, so I volunteered. In third year I became chief engineer, overseeing both mechanical and electrical projects. The car never made it to competition, but I'm proud of several projects. After third year I left to focus on the toboggan team.

Accumulator

The biggest project I finished as chief engineer: a 10 kWh, 48V lithium iron phosphate battery pack with custom copper busbars, distributed battery management, and a fusing system. It stores all the vehicle's energy, and its being unfinished the year before had stalled the project.

  • 10 kWh
  • 48V
  • LiFePO4 cells

Safety circuit boards

The precharge board guards against inrush current. I built it from earlier designs and added an ESP32 to compute the logic the rules require. The HV/LV and TSAI board checks for high voltage directly and lights the LEDs on top of the car, using an optocoupler to isolate the two voltage sides.

Final drive sprocket

To improve drive efficiency I changed the gear ratio, modeled motor operating points in Excel to exceed 90% efficiency for the 80 kW motor, and ran structural FEA in NX on the front sprocket carrier under 150 Nm. I also wrote FreeRTOS code for the ESP32 to verify throttle plausibility over CAN bus. The sprocket was machined by the school's machinist.

  • 80 kW motor
  • over 90% efficiency
  • 150 Nm validated

Great Northern Concrete Toboggan

RolePresident
OrganizationCooper Union Concrete Toboggan Team
TimelineSep 2025 to present

A concrete toboggan is a metal sled that carries five people down Canadian ski slopes on nothing but a concrete slab. It sounded insane, so I joined. For our first race entry I engineered the tow hook, the primary tether for the snowmobile that pulls the sled uphill, cut from aluminum plate on a CNC waterjet, and machined washer plates for the ski mounts.

Awards: Best Performing Toboggan, Best Braking Performance, People's Choice Award, Best New Team. Read Cooper Union's race coverage

  • Front or rear impact: 60 km/hr
  • Rollover: 45 km/hr
  • Side impact: 30 km/hr

As president, I designed the new frame in OnShape and validated it in Ansys Workbench, redesigned the steering system, and helped the club grow by recruiting new members with complementary expertise.

The frame was my first design this complex for manufacturing. I chose steel because it's more weldable than aluminum at my school. Each side can be welded flat on a table, then cross members join them. The new frame is smaller, making shipping more realistic, while weighing about the same as the old aluminum one.

Quantum Entanglement Research

RoleUndergraduate Researcher
OrganizationThe Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art
TimelineSep 2025 to present

Working with a physics faculty member at the Cooper Union, I investigated open quantum system dynamics, focusing on three-qubit systems subject to non-Markovian environmental noise. The research sought to understand how different noisy environments affect quantum coherence and entanglement.

Using MATLAB numerical simulations of time-dependent Hamiltonians, I demonstrated that non-Markovian memory effects preserve tripartite entanglement significantly better than Markovian approximations. I presented these theoretical and numerical findings in a research poster at the 2026 American Physical Society (APS) Global Summit in Denver, Colorado.

Autonomous Sumo Robot

RoleEmbedded systems integration
CourseMechatronics (ME353)
TimelineJan 2026 to May 2026

My team built a fully autonomous sumo robot to force opponents out of a 3-foot ring. To maximize traction within the 5 lb limit, we engineered a one-piece 3D printed PLA chassis with underside channels and a 12V fan that creates downforce. It runs on two 12V brushless planetary gear motors with Shore 20 silicone wheels in the rear and spring-loaded Teflon casters in front.

I programmed the ATmega328P in C to sample the front IR sensors via ADC. The robot detects the ring edge and stays inside, and when it detects an opponent it engages full torque to push them out.

Shell Eco-Marathon

RoleTeam member
OrganizationHigh Efficiency Karlsruhe, HKA
TimelineMay 2026 to Aug 2026
  • 15 cm lower
  • 20% less volume

During my summer abroad I joined High Efficiency Karlsruhe, a Shell Eco-Marathon team, and redesigned and built the mobile workshop transport cart for the hydrogen prototype vehicle. I lowered the cart by 15 cm based on vehicle hardpoints to improve pit ergonomics and reduce fatigue, which cut its internal volume by 20% and saved trailer space.

Using a metal band saw and manual tapping tools, I modified MiniTec 45 mm aluminum extrusions and balsa wood panels, then integrated an onboard roller test rig with a hinged MDF cutout that keeps the tabletop workbench continuous.

Automated Pancake Cooking Machine

RoleMechanical sub-team
CourseDesign and Prototyping (ME211)
TimelineJan 2025 to May 2025

A 12-person team built a machine that turns raw ingredients into cooked pancakes through three synchronized subsystems: dispensing, mixing, and cooking. I led the cooking subsystem, developing an automated dual-sided griddle that cooks both sides at once within a 12-inch footprint. I made the aluminum lid linkage on the lathe and coupled it to a NEMA 17 stepper motor, then calibrated our Arduino timing to a 100-second cycle that coordinates batter deposition and cooking.

Automated Ping Pong Ball Launcher

RoleMechanical and hardware lead
CoursePrinciples of Design (EID103)
TimelineJan 2024 to May 2024

In the spring of my first year, a team of three designed a launcher and return mechanism that sends ping pong balls into a custom hoop that tracks the score. I engineered a motor-driven dual-spring launcher on an aluminum extrusion chassis. We replaced an underpowered 12V motor with a high-torque one driving a custom 3D-printed arm that depresses the spring lever at a fixed 60-degree angle, and added thin 3D-printed retention slots to fix ball obstruction.

We dropped a complex conveyor concept for a 3D-printed funnel and gravity return ramp, which scored consistently into a sensor-instrumented hoop. The project strengthened both my electrical and mechanical skills.
